spec.kitLine: Full Charge → allies Max HP ▲1%, x30
spec.assertion: ≥30 applications reaching stacks=30/maxStacks=30 on ALL 5 allies, never expiring, with a CONSTANT flat value per target. Fails under: passive (1 application), fullBurstEnter (<10, never caps), self-only scope, an uncapped/5-cap stack, and — the subtle one — a compounding basis that recomputes 1% off already-boosted max HP (≈ +35% instead of +30% at cap).
Deleting the Max HP stacks lowers team damage. Fails if the ATK-from-max-HP conversion reads BASE max HP — i.e. if the word "final" is unmodeled and the two skills are wired independently.

Application count/5 equals the fullBurstStart count, the first application PRECEDES the first fullBurstStart in the log, all 5 allies, and stretching 5s→10s strictly raises damage. Fails under fullBurstEnter keying (lands at/after FB open), burstCast keying (he is Burst II and can never enter stage 3 himself, so it would be near-zero), self-scope, and a non-binding/permanent duration.

spec.kitLine: Burst → allies ATK ▲1% of user max HP 15s
spec.assertion: All 5 allies receive the SAME flat value in one dispatch (caster basis), the value GROWS between his first and last burst ("final" max HP), self-scoping it costs team damage, and its expiry frame is exactly 300f later than the co-cast 10s burst buff (15s vs 10s, frame-free). Fails under the nearest-wrong per-target-max-HP basis (five different values — the schema's atkOfMaxHpPct is documented as the target's OWN max HP, so no StatKey cleanly expresses this line), under a base-max-HP snapshot (constant value), and under any 15↔10 duration mix-up.

Self-only target set, maxStacks=5 with the cap actually reached, never expires, and raising the cap to 30 raises HIS damage while leaving every teammate byte-identical. Fails under ally scope, an uncapped stack (he bursts >5 times in 180s), and a timed encoding.

The 7.15% fillGauge exists; removing it strictly reduces the Full Burst count; and retargeting the block from allies to self changes the FB count by ZERO. The last is the ×5 trap guard: the gauge is a single team pool, so a per-target fill would deliver ~25%/s of gauge (a Full Burst every few seconds) — globally impossible.

weaponSwap carries damagePct 350, chargeMultPct 300, maxAmmo 1 and a positive duration, and deleting it costs him damage. Fails if the burst is modeled as a flatDamage rider instead of a weapon change (which would also lose the shot economy the charge-time ladder acts on).

The set of swap chargeTimeSec values is exactly {3, 2.5, 2, 1.5, 0.4}, those blocks are resourceGate'd on ONE shared pool, and flattening every stage to 3s costs damage. Structural + behavioural together: the behavioural half alone passes for a single stage-agnostic charge time, which is the most likely simplification of this line.

Pierce is carried on the weaponSwap (or a gainPierce effect), and the file-level hasPierce flag is NOT true. Fails under whole-fight pierce tagging, which would tag all 180s of his base SR fire instead of just the swap window and over-credit every Pierce Damage ▲ consumer.

All 5 allies receive it, self-scoping it strictly lowers every teammate's total, it lands before the first fullBurstStart (burst-cast timing, not FB-enter), and it expires. Fails under self-scope, fullBurstEnter keying, and a permanent encoding.

fixtures: controlComp('maxwell-ordinary-mechanic', true) for all 10 runs — liter B1 / crown B2 / helm B3 supply the burst chain so Full Bursts actually occur (his stage-3 line and every FB-timed reading are vacuous otherwise), and the fixed B3 slot is kept because none of his lines read a teammate's buffs. Deterministic, no seed. Runs: base + 9 withPatchedOverride counterfactuals (drop fillGauge; retarget fillGauge to self; S1b 5s→10s; Overcurrent cap 5→30; S2a allies→self; B2 allies→self; flatten every swap chargeTimeSec to 3s; delete the weaponSwap; delete the S1a Max HP stacks). DECLARED FIXTURE RISK: he is Burst II and the control comp already holds a Burst II unit (crown), so they compete for the single stage-2 slot. Each burst-keyed group opens with an explicit non-vacuity assertion (he casts at all; >5 times for the Overcurrent cap) — if those go red the fixture starved his cast and the S2a/S2b/B1/B2 groups are VOID rather than refuted; the fix is a comp without a second Burst II.
gaps: burst swap durationSec — the kit states no window length for the UberBuster; ⚑ estimate = 10s (the Full Burst window, corroborated by the burst's own 10s ally buff). Only asserted to be positive; exact value it.skip'd.

swap shot economy — "Max Ammunition Capacity: 1" forces a reload between every shot and the kit is silent on the swap weapon's reload time (⚑ ALWAYS-flag #3). At the stage-5 0.4s charge the reload dominates the shot rate, so the ladder's true damage value is not derivable from prose. it.skip'd.

"Charge Time is fixed" is a stat CLAMP (charge-speed buffs must not shorten it). The schema has chargeSpeedPct but no clamp primitive, so a charge-speed support would illegally accelerate the fixed time. it.skip'd — engine-modeling gap, not an override defect.

S2a stat basis — no StatKey expresses "ATK ▲ x% of the CASTER's final max HP, granted to all allies": atkOfMaxHpPct is documented as the TARGET's own max HP, and casterMaxHpPct grants HP rather than ATK. The live caster-basis equality assertion is the probe for this; if it is red the gap is real and needs a schema addition, not an override edit.

The caster-basis equality assertion assumes the control comp's five units do not all share an identical max HP pool (Attacker/Supporter/Defender differ). If they did, that assertion would pass vacuously.

Overcurrent stage vs the ladder is asserted through a resourceGate pool because the schema offers no other stack-threshold gate; a driver expressing the same ladder via `modes` or a single stage-averaged charge time would fail that structural check while still being arguably faithful — flagged as an encoding, not a magnitude, divergence.
